data.narrative: Devanshi analyzed requirements for the SkillSwap marketplace using a categorized matrix, successfully caught and structured the cancellation policy contradiction, and selected a balanced provider-first policy with platform cooling-off guardrails.

dimension_scores.observation: Identified explicit and implicit stakeholder requirements and isolated contradiction between provider autonomy and learner refund guarantees.
dimension_scores.evidence: Categorized matrix in requirements-matrix.md and proposed Option 2 policy reconciling REQ-03.

dimension_scores.observation: Identified downstream impacted systems for cancellation policy resolution.
dimension_scores.evidence: Flagged payments/escrow, refund processing engine, and provider earnings dashboard as affected systems.

dimension_scores.observation: Recognized risk of vague cancellation policy causing marketplace dispute and booking conflicts.
dimension_scores.evidence: Stated that Option 2 balances provider flexibility with learner protection while acknowledging added logic complexity.

dimension_scores.observation: Structured policy options with concrete rules, impacted parties, and implementation tradeoffs.
dimension_scores.evidence: Defined tiered cancellation and cooling-off period.

dimension_scores.observation: Quickly transitioned from identifying contradiction to proposing workable solution options.
dimension_scores.evidence: Committed to Option 2 with trade-off acknowledgment.

dimension_scores.observation: Mapped how policy rules touch checkout UI, payment gateways, and provider dashboard.
dimension_scores.evidence: Specified affected requirements in Section 3 of requirements matrix.

strengths: Strong awareness of two-sided marketplace dynamics and stakeholder tradeoffs
Recognized engineering complexity tradeoffs in tiered policies vs flat rules
growth_areas: Continue pushing for explicit time window thresholds and edge case definitions upfront
data.recommendation: In Module 2, map dependencies strictly as a DAG to catch circular blockers before sequencing.

public_evidence.student_action: Structured 10 stakeholder requirements and resolved cancellation contradiction by specifying a tiered provider policy with platform cooling-off floor.
public_evidence.proof: Categorized matrix with REQ-01 through REQ-10 and documented downstream impacts on payments and refund logic.
public_evidence.ability: Extracts implicit requirements and resolves specification conflicts
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows ability to turn ambiguous product specs into implementable engineering requirements without blocking teams.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Built categorized requirements matrix for multi-sided marketplace
Selected tiered cancellation policy balancing provider retention against learner protection

teaching_approaches.detail: Grounded platform vs provider autonomy tradeoffs with airline vs Airbnb analogy
